label: mid-prefix (t=3-5) first occurrence of f/s/z/n/l/j after i/w/a/n/0 earlier
explanation: Fires only during the original-input phase, almost entirely at steps t=3-5 (92% of mass; never at t<2, at the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase). Within that window it depends on the token and on what came before: the current input is usually a first occurrence (84% of mass) of a favored token (f strongest at 7x lift, then s, z, n, l, j), and earlier prefix tokens such as i (6x lift as prev/prev2), w, a, n, 0 raise the rate. Top activations look like w i i [n][f] or a i i [f]: f or s at t=3-4 after an i. Digits and tokens like a, b fire rarely. The position-only predicate gets 90% recall but 5% precision, and the conjunction recorded here reaches only about 0.35 F1, so the token and history dependence is graded and spread out rather than a clean rule.
